title: Visual Product Systems Across Web and App
subtitle: Current consumer UI, design-system infrastructure, and the craft to make three digital businesses feel intentional

bio.short: I design the interface and the system that keeps it coherent. At Bibel TV, I combine current consumer UI with color, token, and component infrastructure across mobile, web, connected TV, and Figma. At Ninox and ChurchDesk, I connected design-system decisions, complex workflows, and close Engineering collaboration.
bio.long:
At Bibel TV, I am leading a cross-platform product redesign while remaining hands-on in the interface. The work spans information architecture, interaction, typography, color, light and dark modes, and implementation review across mobile, web, and connected TV. A concept survey challenged the streaming industry's dark default and moved the product toward a warmer, light-first experience.

The visual system is backed by infrastructure. I built an OKLCH color engine that derives readable themes from program artwork, plus Color Lab so Design can tune the behavior without changing code. I also built the token architecture and synchronization that connect product decisions to Figma, Storybook, web, and Android.

At Ninox, I owned the design system, Figma Variables, core components, motion foundations, and joint governance with Engineering. At ChurchDesk, I led design across web and mobile and specified component behavior through annotated flows and redlines. I would bring YOU MAWO strong visual craft for each surface. The same systems judgment can keep three related businesses coherent without making them identical.

context.company: YOU MAWO, One of One, and Additive Scale connect personalized eyewear, software, and additive manufacturing.
context.role: Hands-on UX/UI Designer establishing a shared design library and high-fidelity visual experience across website, app, customer portal, and selected campaign surfaces.
context.emphasis: Show current visual UI before infrastructure: Bibel TV redesign and color system first, followed by Figma, components, tokens, Engineering handoff, and cross-platform governance.
